veranderings.voor: in die derde huis van Akkerstraat en ek ken
veranderings.na: in die derde huis in Akkerstraat, en ek ken
veranderings.rede: A house is 'in' a street, not 'van' it, and the AWS comma is needed before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb.

veranderings.voor: Ons straat is kort en die stoepe
veranderings.na: Ons straat is kort, en die stoepe
veranderings.rede: AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.

veranderings.voor: reg oorkant ons en hulle vas
veranderings.na: reg oorkant ons, en hulle vas
veranderings.rede: AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.

veranderings.voor: is vroeg die oggend moskee toe
veranderings.rede: 'Vroegoggend' is the natural Afrikaans form; 'vroeg die oggend' reads as a translation.
'Later daardie dag' is the idiomatic way to refer back to a day already named.
In AWS spelling a form of address such as 'mev.' takes a small letter in mid-sentence.

veranderings.voor: waarop elke kossoort sy eie plek kry
veranderings.na: waarop elke kossoort sy eie plek gehad het
veranderings.rede: The present tense 'kry' breaks the past-tense narration of the paragraph.
'Platbrood' is written as one compound word.

veranderings.voor: dik boek gelees en die kos
veranderings.na: dik boek gelees, en die kos
veranderings.rede: AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.

veranderings.voor: Ek het gaan groet en hulle
veranderings.na: Ek het gaan groet, en hulle
veranderings.rede: AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.
The separable compound verb 'gereedmaak' is written as one word in the past participle.

veranderings.voor: Ons vier Divali en my ma
veranderings.na: Ons vier Divali, en my ma
veranderings.rede: AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses; the protected word Divali stays unchanged.
A comma separates the leading subordinate clause from the main clause where the two verbs meet.
'Soet lekkers' is redundant, since lekkers are sweet by definition; 'soetgoed' is the natural word for sweet treats.
In Afrikaans you 'sit' a Christmas tree 'op'; 'neergesit' suggests putting something down.
'Daardie oggend' makes clear that this is the morning of Christmas Day.
AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.

vlae.teks: Daarna het die hele gesin onder die boom in die agterplaas geëet.
vlae.rede: 'Die boom' reads as the Christmas tree just mentioned, but that one stands in front of the window, while this one is in the back yard; it is unclear whether a different tree is meant ('n boom), so this is not changed without guessing.
